Marketing.title: Develop Team Riley website positioning for AI Business OS offer
Marketing.details:
Workstream: Team Riley website / agency positioning
Next actor: Joshua
When: none
Priority: normal
Source: Slack planning thread 2026-08-29

Use this planning brief to update the Team Riley website positioning and related offer messaging. Do not publish or change the live site without Joshua’s explicit approval.

Planning brief

Team Riley should not sell “Hermes setup.” Hermes is part of the implementation stack. The core offer is an AI Business Operating System Implementation: identify how a company operates, connect systems and data, build AI agents and automations around workflows, and create an operating layer that reduces manual work while making the business faster, more consistent, and more scalable.

Position the offer as fractional-CTO-level business transformation rather than generic “AI automation.” Suggested central message: “We build an AI operating layer for your company so your people spend less time managing information and more time doing the work only humans should be doing.”

Offer ladder:
• AI Opportunity Audit — interviews, systems/process audit, AI opportunities, roadmap, ROI priorities — $3K–$7.5K.
• AI Automation Build — 1–3 important workflows, integrations, agent(s), testing, documentation — $10K–$15K.
• AI Business OS — implementation across several functions/systems — $25K–$40K.
• Fractional AI CTO — continuous optimization, new agents, integrations, oversight — $3K–$7.5K+/month.

A fully integrated $30K implementation is within the market range for SMB AI projects; larger custom engagements can be scoped at $50K–$100K+ once Team Riley has proof and a repeatable methodology. Price against delivered business value, not effort or hours. Example outcome: a 30-person company saving 150 employee-hours/month at a blended $50/hour yields $7,500/month or $90,000/year before incremental revenue, alongside instant lead responses, marketing drafting/scheduling, sales follow-up monitoring, management reporting, institutional knowledge, meeting preparation, task routing, connected CRM/email/calendar/Slack, and fewer dropped handoffs.

Build the case study on Team Riley itself. Document “Before Hermes: How Team Riley operated” and “After Hermes: What the system handles.” Measure hours saved, response time, tasks automated, marketing output, follow-up consistency, information retrieval, meetings prepared, leads handled, and other concrete operational outcomes.

The eventual proof-led proposition: “I spent six months turning my own agency into an AI-operated company. We documented the architecture, figured out what works and what doesn’t, and now we install that operating model into other businesses.” This moves Team Riley from “guy who builds websites” toward the person who understands and improves the business technology layer.

Do not immediately put a “$30,000 AI package” on the pricing page. Treat this as consultative selling initially: privately offer an AI Transformation Sprint starting at $15,000, then scope larger implementations at $20K, $30K, $50K, and beyond. After two or three real implementations establish a repeatable process, productize the flagship as “Team Riley AI Business OS — $30,000 implementation + $3,000–$5,000/month management.”
